how: We read the website of every Seattle wedding videographer listed on Lazo (123 listings, 94 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: photo booth and 360-booth companies, elopement chapels, an officiant, a wedding planner, photographers whose sites never mention film, and a chain with a landing page per suburb. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: How do you capture vows and toasts over wind and rain? Ask whether audio comes from lapel mics and a board feed, not just the camera.
What arrives and when: a highlight film, a full ceremony edit, toasts, raw footage? Ask for lengths and turnaround in writing.
Is there a cap on hours or locations, and what happens if the ferry or the reception runs late?

picks.name: Boris Studio
picks.blurb: Boris Studio in Shoreline says it has spent over 20 years filming weddings in Seattle, Bellevue, Redmond and beyond, with cinematic films that lean on emotion and artistry. Packages combine video and photo and are customized to the couple.

picks.name: MXBLOOM FILMS LLC
picks.blurb: Neil and Fiona of MXBloom Films are a husband-and-wife team doing wedding photography and cinematography out of Mill Creek, with a second base in Colorado. Storytelling is the center of the pitch: honest, emotional and cinematic, with pricing and packages listed on the site.

picks.name: NWLifeShots
picks.blurb: NW Life Shots offers photo plus video coverage from Bellevue for couples across Seattle and the Pacific Northwest. Robin counts seven-plus years and more than 300 weddings, and is taking inquiries for 2027.

picks.name: Pixel Dust Weddings - Seattle
picks.blurb: Pixel Dust Weddings makes cinematic wedding films for couples across Washington from Seattle. Packages are customizable and typically cover first look through dancing, with a 60- to 90-second sneak peek film delivered for Instagram.

picks.name: BH Films
picks.blurb: BH Films is a Seattle film company that specializes in wedding videography and nothing else. The package lists a professionally edited 8- to 10-minute highlight video with toasts as an added feature, and the team works primarily in Washington but will travel nationwide.

picks.name: Tru Filmmakers
picks.blurb: Tru Filmmakers is a Kent-based team of filmmakers and photographers that describes itself as a group of artists capturing raw moments. Inquiries go through the contact tab after you have looked at the portfolio on the site and Instagram.

picks.name: ECHNO FILMS Wedding Videographer
picks.blurb: Echno Films is one Seattle-area wedding filmmaker who says the job is the most rewarding career there is and takes time to immerse in each couple's day. The site lays out a range of wedding videographer packages, on the belief that every couple's film should be told differently.

picks.name: Seattle Wedding Videographers
picks.blurb: This Tacoma-based team has shot Seattle-area weddings since 2007 in an unobtrusive, documentary style. The listed package is eight hours of multi-camera coverage, a four- to six-minute highlight film, full ceremony and toast edits, raw footage and an online gallery.

picks.name: Lindsey Paradiso Photography
picks.blurb: Lindsey Paradiso pairs documentary wedding photography with films from a Seattle base, promising thoughtful planning and a seamless experience. More than a decade behind the camera, with the FAQ page answering the logistics up front.

picks.name: Jenn Tai & Co
picks.blurb: Jenn Tai & Co offers video alongside its candid, photojournalistic photography, so one Seattle team covers both. Working in Washington and worldwide since 2007, with the family moments called out as the priority.

picks.name: Loc Le Films
picks.blurb: Loc Le Films is a Seattle photographer, a data analyst by day, who adds films for the couples who want them and brings a photobooth to the reception when it makes sense. Based in Des Moines, serving the Pacific Northwest, with a pitch about preserving how the day felt rather than how it looked.
